concept.title: Which file to send
concept.shortdesc: Send a GEDZIP file to anyone who uses uFTi. Send a plain family tree file only to an older program.

conbody.p: To share your tree with someone who uses , save a copy as a GEDZIP file, and send that file. shows how to make one.

A GEDZIP file holds your whole workspace: the tree, its research notes, and the pictures and other attached files. It is one file, so it is easy to attach to an email or to put in a shared folder. Nothing is left behind, so the other person sees what you see. says more.

section.title: For an older program
section.p: Some older programs cannot read a GEDZIP file. For them, save a plain family tree file instead. It holds the people, families, facts, sources and research notes, but not the pictures or other attached files. If the other person needs the pictures, send them as well.

section.title: Do not send the files beside your tree
section.p: Do not send the files that keeps beside your tree. The backup is an old version of your tree. The file written in GEDCOM 7 is a second copy of it. Sending the wrong one sends an old tree or a second copy. says what each file is.
A saved copy stays as it was when you made it. Make a new one before you send, if you have added anything since.
